decisions.decision: retain existing default; no new adoption
decisions.handoff: #39 runs the final 3x100k resource soak against this configuration.
decisions.rationale: It preserves the measured fixed topology and fresh-store isolation. The 7-run default candidate is reference-equivalent to the calibration and confirms the already selected Phase 0 configuration; it does not introduce a new runtime behavior.

decisions.candidate: bounded preparation/cache reuse versus cold preparation
decisions.decision: retain existing setting; no new adoption
decisions.handoff: #9 generalizes the cache key, policy, eviction, and multi-component compatibility proof.
decisions.rationale: The matrix includes a cache-disabled control and the targeted cold-preparation profile. The cache-disabled variant is an explicitly separate Phase 1 experiment, so the existing bounded immutable cache remains the reference setting.
decisions.scope: bounded one-entry prepared-component cache and explicit cache-disabled control

decisions.handoff: #8 owns configuration, fairness, and fixed multi-class capacity policy.
decisions.rationale: The matrix retains fixed ratios as explicitly non-reference Phase 1 experiments and does not select a universal winner.

decisions.handoff: #9 must provide generalized pooling limits, density evidence, and a reset/isolation proof before any production choice.
decisions.rationale: The experiment has an explicit fixed upper bound and no retained linear-memory allowance, but it changes node-fixed mapping and reset behavior; it is not a comparison against the selected reference.

decisions.handoff: #9 owns target-aware Wasmtime policy and must retain a safe non-COW fallback.
decisions.rationale: Linux support is profiled explicitly, but its parallel-memory tradeoff is workload-dependent and belongs to the explicitly separate Phase 1 experiment scope.

decisions.candidate: avoidable activation-path allocations and payload copies
decisions.handoff: #9 owns canonical value mapping; #11 owns activation-envelope/lifecycle ownership and cleanup.
